tasks.title: Suspicious Indicators
tasks.prompt: Read the first email (File 01). Select at least four valid suspicious indicators, then identify the lines supporting four of them. Selecting an incorrect indicator invalidates the answer.

parts.label: Suspicious indicators
parts.hint: Select at least four. Selecting an incorrect indicator invalidates the entire answer.

options.text: The sender's domain resembles the university's official domain but is different.
The button's destination (href) differs from the link displayed in the email.
Urgent, threatening language: “within 24 hours” and “permanent cancellation of the stipend.”
The Reply-To address uses a public free email service and differs from the sender.
A generic greeting, “Dear Student,” without a name.
The email asks the recipient to update information through a link.
The Return-Path and sending server use a domain other than the “Student Affairs” domain.
Many spelling mistakes in the email.
The email arrived in the morning.
The email is written in Arabic.
The email contains an executable attachment.

parts.label: Indicator locations in the file
parts.hint: Select four different lines supporting your chosen indicators.

tasks.title: Why Is spf=pass Not Enough?
tasks.prompt: The first email's header says spf=pass. Select only the correct statements about SPF, DKIM, and DMARC, then identify the Authentication-Results line in the file.

parts.label: Correct statements
parts.hint: Select at least four correct statements. Selecting an incorrect statement invalidates the answer.

options.text: SPF passed for the Return-Path domain, not the From domain.
The Return-Path domain differs from the From domain.
dkim=none means the email has no digital signature.
dmarc=none means no DMARC policy is published for the From domain.
SPF passing shows the server is authorized to send for its domain; it does not prove the email is trustworthy.
spf=pass means the university sent the email.
dkim=none means the signature passed.
dmarc=none means the email passed DMARC.
The email passed the checks, so it is safe.

parts.label: Why does this matter to the attacker?

options.text: To personalize the link with the victim's identity and make the message more convincing.
To prefill the fake login page with the victim's email address.
To track who clicked the link.
Because it encrypts the email so nobody can read it.
Because it is the key for decrypting the rest of the email.
Because it makes the link work without an internet connection.

parts.label: Correct statements

options.text: The lookalike domain was registered just four days before the incident.

tasks.prompt: Write a two-sentence assessment covering the attack type, the attacker's objective, and their likely next step. The mentor will grade it.
